parts:
Thanks Joe, My ui.r starts as follows:

shinyUI({require(shinyGridster);bootstrapPage(  

And tailed with a brace } of course.  This actually does work.   I suppose it's obvious (at least, it is at the start of the day)!
  • Is it the correct idiom? 
  • Is it documented, or more in general is there a sequence diagram somewhere that would help me understand object interaction/timelines so I don't ask too many dumb questions?
  • Open question: are folks using shinyGridster, am I barking up the wrong tree? I like it and want it...
  • Can I get a grey (or indeed gray) backgound so my white background grid panes can be visually cued as 'objects' or 'panes'?
Apart from that and referring to shiny itself, I get intermittent 'shockwave crashed :(' problems googleVis which crash the object, not shiny, especially when I click the 'line plot' tab, so I'm kind of giving up on googleVis for now... not your problem, I know, but maybe some other users have comments or workarounds.

I use an animated slider instead, which works but but it has a couple of UE issues: (1) fine locally, but clunky remotely for any multi-pane graphics (OK, I know, it's asking a lot - but that's where googleVis excels with it's interpolation/anti-aliasing) (2) Can't seem to control the speed other than changing the 'step' argument on the slider.

This is all fine-tuning, really.  

Oh, did I say, what a cool thing is shiny?!  Life-enhancing.

Giles

messages.subject: Re: shiny-gridster
parts: This is some answers from a Shiny amataur
• Is it the correct idiom?

require(shinyGridster); can also be placed outside of shinyUI like so

require(shinyGridster); 
shinyUI( bootrapPage( ....

Please correct me if my shiny-understanding is wrong. Placing it outside will run it once per run of runApp(), whereas as placing it inside shinyUI runs the require(shinyGridster) everytime the page is refreshed in the browser or you open up another browser tab/window and you connect to the server. Probably doesn't make a difference for something innocuous like require() but this understanding might be useful for other things
• Is it documented, or more in general is there a sequence diagram somewhere that would help me understand object interaction/timelines so I don't ask too many dumb questions?

• I believe you can put options(shiny.reactlog=TRUE);  in your server.R code. And when you are using the browser just press Ctrl-F3 to bring out the reactive log, maybe that will help you out
    • Or you may want to look into this blog post http://blog.analytixware.com/2013/09/visualising-shiny-reactive-dependencies.html
• Open question: are folks using shinyGridster, am I barking up the wrong tree? I like it and want it...
• I think it's really cool but I had some problem making it work with my current layout as I am new to HTML/CSS and so I believe I am not qualified to answer the next question
• Can I get a grey (or indeed gray) backgound so my white background grid panes can be visually cued as 'objects' or 'panes'?

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: shiny-gridster
parts: Comments inline

On Thu, Sep 12, 2013 at 10:44 PM, Giles Heywood <gilesh...@gmail.com> wrote:
Thanks Joe, My ui.r starts as follows:

shinyUI({require(shinyGridster);bootstrapPage(  

And tailed with a brace } of course.  This actually does work.   I suppose it's obvious (at least, it is at the start of the day)!
  • Is it the correct idiom?

Not really, the normal idiom is just to call library(shinyGridster) at the top of ui.R. Your way works equally well but is harder to read and it's also nice to be able to look at the top of the file to see what libraries are depended on.
• Is it documented, or more in general is there a sequence diagram somewhere that would help me understand object interaction/timelines so I don't ask too many dumb questions?
Not really, if you're asking how ui.R and server.R are loaded and how shinyUI/shinyServer are implemented. If you haven't read the scoping chapter of the tutorial, that may help.
• Open question: are folks using shinyGridster, am I barking up the wrong tree? I like it and want it...
The package was developed by one of the Shiny maintainers and will likely become "official" at some point in the future, so as far as non-Shiny-core components go, it's a pretty safe bet.
• Can I get a grey (or indeed gray) backgound so my white background grid panes can be visually cued as 'objects' or 'panes'?

Yes, you can just use CSS for that. Include this somewhere in your shinyUI (replace #888888 with whatever shade of grey you want):

tags$style(type="text/css", "body { background-color: #888888; }")

Apart from that and referring to shiny itself, I get intermittent 'shockwave crashed :(' problems googleVis which crash the object, not shiny, especially when I click the 'line plot' tab, so I'm kind of giving up on googleVis for now... not your problem, I know, but maybe some other users have comments or workarounds.

You could try my bindings, they use a different approach to integrate googleVis with Shiny that should be more robust if these crashes have to do with reactivity causing the plots to be updated. (At some point in the future you'll see these bindings integrated into the googleVis package proper, once I have a little more time.)

I use an animated slider instead, which works but but it has a couple of UE issues: (1) fine locally, but clunky remotely for any multi-pane graphics (OK, I know, it's asking a lot - but that's where googleVis excels with it's interpolation/anti-aliasing) (2) Can't seem to control the speed other than changing the 'step' argument on the slider.

I'm not clear on what you mean by #1. For #2, see ?animationOptions; you can use this instead of TRUE when passing the animate argument to sliderInput. One of the options it lets you set is the interval.

This is all fine-tuning, really.  

Oh, did I say, what a cool thing is shiny?!  Life-enhancing.
Thanks :)

Giles
